name: Knee to chest
movement: lying on the back, one knee hugged to the chest and held, the other leg flat

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you.

words.hint: Lying on your back, one knee hugged in to the chest and held, the other leg flat.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie on your back side on to it and hug one knee in to your chest.
words.position: Lie on your back side on to the phone, the working leg nearest it. Hug that knee in toward the chest with both hands behind the thigh; the other leg stays flat on the floor.
words.top: The knee drawn in close to the chest, the hands behind the thigh, the other foot on the floor, the head and shoulders down, held.
howto: Lie on your back, both knees bent with the feet flat — or the other leg straight if that is comfortable.
Bring one knee up and hug it in toward the chest with both hands behind the thigh, just below the knee, until a stretch is felt in the lower back and the buttock.
Hold for the count, breathing slowly, with the head and shoulders resting on the floor and the other foot down.
Lower the leg slowly, then the other side.
words.cannot: How the lower back feels and where the hands hold — behind the thigh, not over the kneecap: it sees how close the knee is, the other foot staying down and the head and shoulders staying on the floor.
words.about: Knee to chest — lying on the back side on: the hug, as the angle at the hip between the shoulder and the knee, at most 75° (the leg flat is 180; full hip bend is about 60); the other foot staying on the floor, whether that leg is straight or bent; the shoulders not curling up off the floor (the hip-to-shoulder line within 8° of the start) and the head resting down (within 15°). The clock runs while the hug, the other foot and the shoulders are right. Thirty seconds a hold, three holds each side.
words.lost: Lie on your back side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.hold: That is it — hold and breathe
words.safety: A stretch, not a strain: hold behind the thigh, not over the kneecap. Stop if the pain travels down the leg. With osteoporosis, ask your physio first: curling the spine forward is often advised against.
words.easier: The other knee bent with the foot flat; a shorter hold; less pull.
words.harder: A longer hold; the knee drawn a little closer; both knees together.
words.mistakes: Curling the head and shoulders up to meet the knee; the other leg lifting; pulling on the shin or kneecap; bouncing; holding the breath.

measurements.label: knee to chest
measurements.why: The angle at the hip between the shoulder and the knee: 180 lying flat, about 60 at full hip bend. 75 or less is a close hug.
